To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the concept of collapsibility, which is a generalization of the concept of consistency, can be used as a tool to derive tractability results for QCSPs and (b) the concept of consistency is a special case of collapsibility.

(1) the concept of consistency can be generalized to the quantified setting, (2) this generalization can be further refined into two distinct concepts of collapsibility and consistency, and (3) these two concepts, together with a few simple properties of the quantified relations, are sufficient to prove tractability of the QCSP and provide algorithms for the tractable cases.

(a) a new concept, called collapsibility, provides an elegant unification of tractability results for certain QCSPs, (b) collapsibility is a generalization of a concept, called consistency, which is used to prove tractability of certain CSPs, (c) the notion of consistency can be used to derive a new tractability result for a class of CSPs which has not previously been considered in the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the complexity of QCSPs where the allowed relations are restricted in some way?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the classes of QCSPs that are tractable are those in which there are no cycles of relations that can be used to form a non-true inconsistent set of constraints, and in which all relations can be used to make a true inconsistent set of constraints.
the QCSP is tractable when all relations are either (1) symmetric, or (2) symmetric and have a finite domain, or (3) symmetric and have an infinite domain.
the QCSP is tractable if all quantifier-free constraints are consistent or collapsible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for any class of tractable QC-SATs, there is an algorithm that solves the corresponding class of tractable QCS-SATs.
the QCSPs that are tractable are those in which there is some form of "collapsibility", which we formalize as a generalization of consistency.
, in the context of QCSP, the concept of consistency is not a useful notion for characterising tractability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notions of collapsibility and consistency are complementary.
, by considering two new concepts, one can unify and extend the existing results for the QCSP, and derive new tractability results and corresponding algorithms.
the concepts of collapsibility and consistency are useful for studying the complexity of the QCSP.
